text:
Alex Kim: Quick UX review request — thinking about the trace viewer's error drilldown. Current mock puts the 'Export trace' action in the kebab menu (top right). Feels hidden when you're investigating incidents. cc @Maria Gomez for design context

Maria Gomez: Agree — export is a primary action during postmortems. If it's in a 3-dot menu people won't find it under stress. Can we try a left-aligned icon button next to the trace title? :mag:

Jin Park: Left-aligned button works visually but watch horizontal space. Traces with long titles wrap. Maybe show icon-only on narrow screens and full "Export trace" label on wider widths?

Priya Nair: Accessibility nit: if we add an icon-only button, we need visible focus and an aria-label. Also keyboard shortcut would be great — something like 'E' when the trace panel has focus.

Sam Lee: For implementation FYI — export generates a zipped bundle: trace.json, associated logs, and request metadata. We can stream a signed URL back once bundle ready. That matches current backend. No blocking work.

Maria Gomez: Mock: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/trace-ux?node-id=210%3A12 — created two variants: A) primary export button next to title, B) icon-only in the header with tooltip. Which do folks prefer?

Alex Kim: Leaning to A (labelled) for discoverability. But, can label be truncated to 'Export' (not 'Export trace') to save space?

Priya Nair: "Export" is okay if tooltip expands to 'Export trace (includes logs & request metadata)'. Also add role="button" and aria-describedby that references the tooltip text for screen readers. Ensure the zip file name includes the correlation ID.

Jin Park: UX question: when you click Export, do we show a toast only or a modal with granular options (include logs, stack traces, timeframe)? I think modal might be useful for advanced users.

Maria Gomez: Good point — added a compact modal variant in figma. Default Export = include full trace + logs. Advanced ▼ opens checkboxes for stack traces, raw spans, and related requests. Keeps default quick while supporting deep dives.

Sam Lee: Backend already records request correlation ID as "corr_id" in metadata. Will make filename: trace-<corr_id>-<ts>.zip. Also we can produce a small MD5 checksum file inside for integrity.

Alex Kim: Copy tweak suggestion for modal confirm button: change from 'Download' to 'Download trace bundle' to reduce ambiguity. Thoughts?

Maria Gomez: I think "Download trace bundle" is long visually. How about primary label 'Download' and secondary helper text under the checkboxes: 'Bundle includes trace.json, logs, and metadata'.

Jin Park: +1 for that. Also accessibility: ensure modal traps focus and returning focus to the export button on close

Priya Nair: Keyboard flow: focus order should be Export button -> modal -> first checkbox -> action buttons. Add aria-live region for progress updates when the bundle is being generated so screen readers know about long-running exports.

Maria Gomez: UX decision summary: primary labelled export button next to title (responsive to icon-only on narrow widths); compact modal for advanced options; tooltip + aria text for icon-only; toast + aria-live updates during generation; filename includes correlation ID. I'll update figma and add microcopy.

Alex Kim: Sweet. Can someone post final figma link + a tiny checklist for eng on required ARIA attrs and keyboard shortcut? I'll own the follow-up ticket and add acceptance criteria.

Sam Lee: I'll add backend filename and signed URL details to the ticket. Also add an API endpoint: POST /internal/traces/export { trace_id, options } -> 202 Accepted with job_id. Poll GET /internal/traces/export/{job_id} for status.

design-bot: Reminder: design review sync at 4pm today if you want to walk through interactions :calendar:
notes: Decisions: labelled export button, modal for options, accessibility requirements (aria-label, aria-live, focus trap), filename includes corr_id. Owners: Alex (follow-up ticket), Maria (figma + microcopy), Sam (backend API).
